IFS response to the guaranteed-work-placement element for young people on long-term benefits:
- Policy: guarantee paid work for every young person on Universal Credit for 18 months without being in education or employment; those who refuse a placement without a "reasonable excuse" face sanctions, including potentially losing benefits. Around 100,000 young people are out of paid work, have been on UC at least a year, and are required to look for work — the group most likely in scope.
- IFS: key test is whether it helps young people into sustained jobs, not just temporary placements. The earlier Kickstart scheme (voluntary subsidised employment for 16-24s on UC) helped roughly one in ten participants into sustained employment two years later, even on optimistic assessments.
- Requiring employer co-funding raises the chance placements give genuine experience but also raises the bar to employer participation, for a programme reliant on employer engagement.

VERBATIM QUOTE:
Imran Tahir, Senior Research Economist at IFS: "Unemployment at young ages can leave lasting scars on careers and earnings. Yet young people who have been unemployed for a long time are also among the hardest groups to support."
